en: The phonetic instruction on the letters consists of the designations of male, female, and neuter for the consonants;
namely, the letter *ka*, the letter *ga*, the letter *ca*, and the letter *ja*.
The letter *ṭa*, the letter *ḍa*, the letter *ta*, and the letter *da*;
the letter *pa*, the letter *ba*, the letter *ṣa*, and the letter *kṣa*—
these twelve phonemes are proclaimed to be masculine.
The letter *kha*, the letter *gha*, the letter *cha*, the letter *jh*,
the letter *ṭha*, the letter *ḍha*, the letter *tha*, the letter *dha*,
the letter *pha*, the letter *bha*, the letter *śa*, and the letter *sa*.
These indeed are proclaimed as the "seeds of light" (bhānu-bīja) and the "wives" (jāyā);
the remainder is to be known as neuter. Thus, three types are traditionally recorded.
Furthermore, there are thirteen [deities]: Śiva, Agni, Bhūta, Rudra, and the lunar days (tithi).

These indeed are the vowels and consonants (svaravarṇa) proclaimed as being masculine; [the groups] are five, six, twelve, fourteen, eleven, and eighteen. These vowels and consonants are proclaimed as being feminine.
The Prakṛti consists of seven phonemes, while the Vikṛti consists of nine phonemes (7). The Prakṛti is said to be the short vowel, and the Vikṛti is called the long vowel;
[the remaining letters are] the first and third [sibilants], the letter ṣa, and the letter kṣa (8).
These twelve phonemes are proclaimed to be masculine;
likewise, the second, the fourth, and the two *śa*-sounds—
these twelve phonemes are proclaimed to be feminine.
The qualities of sattva, rajas, and tamas belong to the vowels;
likewise, the semi-vowels (antasthā), the sibilants (uttama), as well as the letters ṛ and ḷ,
and the letters ha and la, are proclaimed to be neuter (klība).
The fortnight, the number of houses, and likewise the thirteenth lunar day (11);
these indeed are the qualities of Sattva, as well as the white color; the auspicious ocean, the seven, the earth, the directions, the Rudras, the lunar day, and likewise the digits (12).
These indeed are the qualities of Rajas; likewise, the red color, the arrow, the taste, and the third, the dark color, are the quality of Tamas. 13. Hal.
The second and fourth [letters], the first and last of the *tavarga*,
the first of the *pavarga*, as well as the fourteenth and eighteenth—
these indeed possess the quality of *sattva* and are likewise white in color. 14.
The letter *kha*, the letter *gha*, the letter *ṭha*, the letter *tha*, the letter *ta*, the letter *na*, the letter *pa*, the letter *pha*,
the letter *va*, the letter *ha*, and the letter *kṣa*— these constitute the *sāttvika*. 15–16.

The first letter of the *ka*-group, the *ṭa*-group, the third letters of the *ta* and *pa* groups, the fourth letters of the *ca* and *ṭa* groups, as well as the last letters of the *ca* and *ṭa* groups,
the sibilants (*ūṣman*), the letter *ra*, and the letters *la* and *la*— these belong to the quality of *rajas*.
The first letter of the *ka*-group (*ka*) and likewise the *ṭa*-group; the third letters [of the *ca*- and *ta*-groups] (*ja* and *da*), as well as the letters *bha*, *dha*, and *ña*;
the letter *ṇa*, the sibilants (*ūṣman*), and likewise *ra* and *la*. 18–19.
These are declared to be the qualities of *rajas*, as well as the color red; likewise, the letter *ca*, the second [consonant], the letter *ṅa*, the letter *ma*, the letter *ḍha*,
the letter *da*, the letter *ya*, and the letter *jha*.
The *tāmasa* [mantra] is black in color, while the *uttama* is mixed.
The second vowel is the letter 'ca'; the first and last letters of the fifth class, the fourth letters of the *ca*-class and *ṭa*-class, and the third letter of the *ta*-class. 21–22.

The letter *ya* is dark-complexioned, possessing the quality of *sattva* and the *sāman* chant. Likewise, the letter *a* has all the deities as its presiding divinity, is red in color, and is known as *rajas*.
The letter *ā* is the supreme power (*parā-śakti*), white in color, and is said to be *sāttvika*.
The letter *i* has Viṣṇu as its deity; it is dark and said to be of the nature of *tamas*.
The letter *ī* is called the power of *māyā*; it is yellow and said to be of the nature of *rajas*.
The letter *u* has Vāstu as its deity; it is black and declared to be of the nature of *tamas*.
The letter *ū* has the Earth as its deity; it is dark-colored and characterized by *tamas*. The letter *ṛ* is to be known as belonging to Brahmā; it is said to be yellow and characterized by *rajas*.
The letter *ṝ* has the form of Śikhaṇḍin; it is yellow in color and characterized by *rajas*.
The Aśvins are said to be *lṛ* and *lṝ*;
the syllable *e* is Vīrabhadra. Yellow *rajas* indeed bestows success;
one should know the syllable *ai* to be Vāgbhava.

One should know the syllable *o* as Īśvara, the light that is sattva and bestows fruit. The syllable *au* is the primordial Śakti, white in color and granting success everywhere. The syllable *aṃ*, however, is Maheśa, red in color and characterized by rajas. 29–30.
The syllable *Aḥ* and Kālarudra are said to be red and characterized by *rajas*; the syllable *Ka*, pertaining to Prajāpati, is yellow and bestows rain as *rajas*.
The syllable *Kha* is the seed-mantra of the Gaṅgā, white as milk and the destroyer of sins.

The syllable *ga* is the lord of the *gaṇas*, red in appearance, and the destroyer of obstacles (32). The syllable *gha* is to be known as Bhairava, pearl-white in appearance, and the destroyer of enemies.
The syllable *ṅa* is the seed-syllable of Time (*kāla*); it is declared to be Kāla-Tārkṣya (33).
The syllable *ca* is Caṇḍarudra; it is the color of collyrium and is characterized by tamas.
The syllable *cha* is Bhadrakālī; she is proclaimed to be tamasic. The syllable *ja* is to be known as Jambhahā (the slayer of Jambha); it is red in appearance and brings victory.
The syllable *jhakāra* is Ardhanārīśa, dark-blue and red, a mixture of the two; 35.
*Ñakāra* has the serpent as its deity, is yellow, and has the form of Rajas; *ṭṭakāra* is Bhṛṅgīśa, red, and likewise identical to Rajas. 36.
The syllable *ṭha* is the seed-syllable of the Moon; it is white and said to be of the *sāttvika* nature.
The syllable *ḍa* is Ekanetra; it is yellow and said to be of the *rājasa* nature.
(37) The syllable *ḍha* is the seed-syllable of Yama; it is blue and destroys death.
The letter Ṇa is the seed-syllable of Nandin; it is red in luster and bestows the accomplishment of one's aims.
The letter Ta has Vāstu as its presiding deity and is white;
the letter Tha is to be known as belonging to Brahmā.
The seed-syllable of Durgā is the letter *da*, which is dark blue in color and bestows the accomplishment of all aims.
The letter *dha* is declared to be the giver of wealth, yellow in appearance, and the granter of success in one's objectives.
The letter *na* is Sāvitrī herself, crystal-like in hue and the destroyer of sins. (39–40)
The syllable *pa* is Parjanya, white in luster and bestowing the accomplishment of rain;
the syllable *pha* is Pāśupata, which destroys the sins of living beings. The syllable *ba* is Trimūrti, yellow in color and bestowing the accomplishment of all aims.
One should know the letter *bha* as belonging to Bhārgava; it is red in color and bestows good fortune. 42 One should know the letter *ma* as Madana; it is dark blue and bestows the fruits of desire.
The letter *ya* has Vāyu as its deity; it is black and effects eradication. 43
The syllable *ra* has Agni as its presiding deity; it is red in appearance and belongs to the *rājasa* quality.
The syllable *la* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*) of the Earth; it is yellow and brings about attainment.
The syllable *va* is the seed-syllable of Varuṇa; it is white in appearance and destroys [the obstacles to] yoga.
The seed-syllable of Lakṣmī is the letter Śa; it is golden-hued and of the nature of Rajas.
The letter Ṣa is the twelve-fold self; it is red-hued and bestows victory.
The letter Sa is the seed-syllable of Śakti; it is red and brings about stability.
The letter *ha* is the seed-syllable of Śiva; it resembles pure crystal and bestows the eight supernatural powers beginning with *aṇiman*, as well as worldly enjoyment and liberation.
The letter *la* is the seed-syllable of the Self (*ātman*); it has a reddish luster and grants all accomplishments.
Thus ends the instruction on phonemes.
